newsitem.title: FRANCE: OLYMPICS-LILLE DISAPPOINTED BUT FEEL EFFORT NOT WASTED.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-LILLE DISAPPOINTED BUT FEEL EFFORT NOT WASTED.

text.p: Double Olympic sprint champion Marie-Jose Perec, mascot for Lille's 2004 Games bid, encapsulated French disappointment at the northern city's failure to reach the short list on Friday.
"Oh no, I don't believe it," Perec exclaimed with a mixture of surprise and anger when Lille did not figure among the five candidates, Athens, Buenos Aires, Cape Town, Rome and Stockholm.
But Lille's mayor Pierre Mauroy, who was in Lausanne for the International Olympic Committee vote, promised "there will be new adventures".
Lille feels it can benefit from the publicity generated by its bid to stage the Games.

"This challenge has allowed the region to validate a strategy of development after the (building of the) Channel tunnel, with the ... Olympic ambition," said Francis Ampe, general secretary of the Lille 2004 bidding committee.
French Sports Minister Guy Drut said: "Lille should not be embarrased by this defeat, especially against great capitals."
